title: B-trees are wide because disks think in pages
body: A B-tree node is sized to a disk page, so one read fetches hundreds of keys and the tree over millions of rows stays three or four levels deep. Depth, not comparisons, is what a database pays for. The design, from Bayer and McCreight in 1970, is hardware-shaped in a way balanced binary trees are not.
source_hint: Bayer and McCreight (1970); database internals literature
